text: Every single lesson so far in this entire course has happened inside Power BI Desktop, on your own machine. Starting right now, the other half of Power BI — the service — takes over as the main subject for the rest of this chapter.

Desktop is where you connect to data, clean it up in Power Query, build out the model, write DAX measures, and design report pages. It's a local authoring tool, full stop — everything you've built lives on your own machine until you publish it somewhere else entirely.

That somewhere else is the Power BI service, at app dot powerbi dot com — a website, not a program you install at all. It's where finished work actually gets stored, refreshed on a schedule automatically, and shared with people who may never open Desktop in their entire career.

Five concepts run straight through this entire chapter, and every remaining lesson digs into one of them. The workspace holds everything together. The semantic model is what your reports actually get built from. The report itself is what you've been designing in Report view all along. Dashboards pin tiles from one or more reports. And apps package all of it up for a genuinely broad audience to consume.

One detail worth remembering: you can't create a workspace from inside Desktop at all — that only ever happens in the browser. Lesson 68 starts with the license question, because what you're actually allowed to do here depends on more than just clicking the right button.
